newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares edge up on moderate Western demand.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares edge up on moderate Western demand.

text.p: Leading Russian shares edged up further on moderate Western demand but foreign investors are still waiting for more news about President Boris Yeltsin's health, traders said.
At 1400 GMT LUKoil was $10.38 after $10.16 at Tuesday's close, UES was $0.0842 after $0.0834, Rostelekom edged up to $2.62 from $2.60 and Surgutneftegaz was $0.397 after $0.396.
Yeltsin was in a satisfactory condition after Tuesday's open heart operation, the Kremlin said.
"Investors are waiting," said Boris Shvedsky, a broker form IK Aton. "When Yeltsin is back on his feet and in his office, we shall be ready for a new push up."
Traders marked share prices up by three to four percent after the Kremlin said that Yeltsin was recovering well and was taken off his lung-machine.

"Some political risk still remains," said Ivan Deraybin, a trader from IFCI-Moscow Partners. "In the morning there were companies which believed in the growth. People were just overexcited. You can still feel the tension on the market."
